name: Performance tuning
purpose: Agentic AI systems, while powerful, often face challenges in consistent, reliable, and cost-effective operation in real-world scenarios. Performance tuning addresses these issues by maximizing resource utilization, reducing latency, improving accuracy, and ensuring scalability. This is crucial for achieving desired business outcomes and user satisfaction, especially as agents handle more complex, multi-step tasks.
coreComponents: Large Language Models (LLMs) and underlying models
Tools, APIs, and external systems integration
Memory management and context retention (e.g., vector databases)
Data curation, quality, and context engineering
keyCapabilities: Improved task adherence and completion rates
Enhanced tool call accuracy and efficiency
integrations: AI Agent Development Kits (ADKs) and Frameworks (e.g., LangChain, Microsoft Autogen, CrewAI)
Observability and monitoring platforms (e.g., AgentOps, TensorBoard, Prometheus, Grafana)
Vector databases for long-term memory and retrieval
Cloud AI services (e.g., Azure AI Evaluation, Google Cloud Vertex AI, AWS Bedrock)
External APIs, microservices, and legacy systems
CI/CD pipelines for continuous integration and deployment
useCases: Customer service automation (optimizing response time, accuracy, and resolution rates)
Financial risk assessment (improving accuracy and efficiency in analyzing complex data)
Automated software engineering (optimizing code generation, testing, and deployment)
Supply chain management (enhancing planning efficiency and resource allocation)
Healthcare (reducing medication errors, improving diagnostic accuracy)
Content generation and summarization (reducing hallucination rates, improving relevance)
